questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Housing loans given at 'teaser rates' (comparatively low rates in the first few years, reset higher later) attract what standard asset provision under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025?

solution.concept: Standard asset provision on teaser-rate housing loans
solution.explanation: Because of their higher risk, housing loans at teaser rates carry a 2.00% standard asset provision. It reverts to 0.40% one year after the rates are reset higher, if the account stays standard.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.25% is for individual housing, farm and SME loans; 0.40% is the general rate (and the rate after reversion); 1.00% is for commercial real estate.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 2.00 per cent

fact_checks.claim: The standard asset provisioning on the outstanding amount of housing loans at teaser rates ... shall be 2.00 per cent ... The provisioning on these assets shall revert to 0.40 per cent after one year from the date on which the rates are reset at higher rates if the accounts remain 'standard'

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, how often must collateral such as immovable property charged to the bank be valued in the case of NPAs with a balance of ₹5 crore and above?

solution.concept: Valuation of collateral of large NPAs
solution.explanation: For NPAs with a balance of ₹5 crore and above, collateral such as immovable properties charged to the bank must be valued once in three years by valuers appointed under Board-approved guidelines.
steps: Collateral valuation → once in three years
solution.why_others_wrong: Annual intervals apply to the stock audit of such NPAs, not to collateral valuation; five years and six months are not the prescribed periods.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Once in three years

fact_checks.claim: In cases of NPAs with balance of ₹5 crore and above, collateral such as immovable properties charged in favour of the bank shall be valued once in three years by valuers appointed as per the guidelines approved by the Board of Directors

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, banks must submit a weekly report of instances of default by all borrowers with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above. By when is this report due?

options.text: By close of business every Monday
Within seven days of each default
On the last working day of each month
By close of business every Friday (or the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday)

solution.concept: Weekly reporting of defaults to CRILC
solution.explanation: Besides monthly CRILC reporting of credit information (including SMA status) on borrowers with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above, banks submit a weekly report of defaults by all such borrowers by close of business every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday.
steps: Weekly default report → close of business every Friday
solution.why_others_wrong: Monday, a seven-day rolling window and month-end are not the stated timing; the monthly cycle is for CRILC credit information, not the weekly default report.
solution.final_answer: Option D: By close of business every Friday (or the preceding working day if Friday is a holiday)

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall submit a weekly report of instances of default by all borrowers (with aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore and above) by close of business on every Friday, or the preceding working day if Friday happens to be a holiday

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For loans sanctioned on or after 31 December 2021, RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025 require certain details to be clearly specified in the loan agreement. Which of the following is among them?

options.text: The realisable value of the security at each future balance sheet date
Examples of the dates on which the account would be classified as SMA or NPA
The provision the bank will make if the account becomes doubtful
The name of the asset reconstruction company to which the loan may be sold

solution.explanation: The loan agreement must clearly specify the exact due dates for repayment, the frequency of repayment, the break-up between principal and interest, examples of dates of SMA/NPA classification, and (for loans with a moratorium) the exact date of commencement of repayment. The borrower must be told of these at sanction and at later changes.
steps: Repayment start date where there is a moratorium
solution.why_others_wrong: Future security values, provisioning plans and potential ARC buyers are not required contents of the agreement.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Examples of the dates on which the account would be classified as SMA or NPA

fact_checks.claim: The exact due dates for repayment of a loan, frequency of repayment, breakup between principal and interest, examples of dates of classification as special mention account (SMA) / non-performing asset (NPA), etc. shall be clearly specified in the loan agreement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's standard project finance book (all projects reached financial closure after 1 October 2025) has: a commercial real estate (CRE) project under construction, ₹400 crore; a CRE–residential housing (CRE-RH) project under construction, ₹200 crore; and an infrastructure project in its operational phase (repaying interest and principal), ₹500 crore. Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, what general provision must it hold on these?

solution.explanation: Project finance attracts portfolio-level general provisions by phase: construction phase – CRE 1.25%, CRE-RH 1.00%, all others 1.00%; operational phase – CRE 1.00%, CRE-RH 0.75%, all others 0.40%. So: 400 × 1.25% = 5.0; 200 × 1.00% = 2.0; 500 × 0.40% = 2.0; total ₹9.0 crore.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹7.5 crore applies operational-phase rates throughout; ₹12.0 crore applies construction-phase rates throughout; ₹8.0 crore uses 0.50% for CRE-RH, which is not a prescribed rate.
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹9.0 crore

fact_checks.claim: For project finance exposures, a bank shall maintain a general provision at the following rates ... Construction Phase / Operational Phase: CRE 1.25 1.00; CRE-RH 1.00 0.75; All others 1.00 0.40
The provisions stipulated ... shall not be applicable for projects where financial closure has been achieved as on October 1, 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025:
I. When a loan is taken over by another bank, the taking-over bank must classify it as NPA from the actual date on which it became NPA, even though it was not in its books on that date.
II. If a bank's on-lending facility to a Primary Agricultural Credit Society is in default, all direct loans by the bank to that society's member-borrowers also become NPA.
III. If overdues from a client's forward contract with the bank become NPA, all other funded facilities of that client are also classified as NPA.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: Under takeout finance, the taking-over bank classifies the asset as NPA from the actual date of it becoming NPA. For PACS/FSS on-lending, only the particular facility to the PACS that is in default is NPA; direct loans to a member outside the on-lending arrangement become NPA only if one of that member's own facilities becomes NPA. Overdues from forward contracts, swaps and options that become NPA drag all other funded facilities of the client into NPA (borrower-wise classification).
steps: II: wrong (PACS default does not by itself make members' direct loans NPA)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options including II are wrong; II overstates the PACS rule.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: Subsequent to take over by a bank, the taking over bank shall classify the asset as NPA from the actual date of it becoming NPA even though the account was not in its books as on that date

only that particular credit facility granted to PACS / FSS which is in default ... The other direct loans and advances, if any, granted by the bank to the member borrower of a PACS / FSS outside the on-lending arrangement shall become NPA even if one of the credit facilities granted to the same borrower becomes NPA
In case the overdues arising from forward contracts and plain vanilla swaps and options become NPAs, all other funded facilities granted to the client shall also be classified as NPA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A borrower's account (lenders' aggregate exposure ₹700 crore at implementation) was restructured and has performed satisfactorily through the monitoring period. To support an upgrade, the borrower obtains normal bank-loan ratings from three RBI-accredited rating agencies: BBB, BBB- and BB+. Under RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, can the account be upgraded?

options.text: Yes; two investment-grade ratings are required and the borrower has two
Yes; only one investment-grade rating is needed for exposures above ₹500 crore
No; upgrade needs an independent credit evaluation of RP1, not ratings
No; when more ratings than required are obtained, all must be investment grade (BBB- or better), and BB+ is not

solution.explanation: For accounts with aggregate exposure of ₹100 crore and above, an upgrade needs, besides satisfactory performance, investment-grade ratings (BBB- or better) of the credit facilities: two ratings for ₹500 crore and above, one below that. If more ratings than required are obtained, all of them must be investment grade. These are normal ratings, not the ICE used for implementing plans. Here BB+ is below investment grade, so the account cannot be upgraded.
steps: Three obtained → all must be ≥ BBB-
solution.why_others_wrong: Having two good ratings is not enough once a third is obtained; above ₹500 crore two ratings are needed; ICE symbols apply to implementing plans, not upgrade.
solution.final_answer: Option D: No; when more ratings than required are obtained, all must be investment grade (BBB- or better), and BB+ is not

fact_checks.claim: for accounts where the aggregate exposure of specified lenders is ₹100 crore and above ... the credit facilities of the borrower shall also be rated as investment grade (BBB- or better) ... accounts with aggregate exposure of ₹500 crore and above shall require two ratings, those below ₹500 crore shall require one rating

if the ratings are obtained from more than the required number of credit rating agencies, all such ratings shall be investment grade for the account to qualify for an upgrade ... These ratings ... shall be the normal ratings provided by the credit rating agencies and not Independent Credit Evaluation

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Loans to distressed persons (other than distressed farmers) to prepay their debt to non-institutional lenders qualify as priority sector under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025 up to what amount per borrower?

solution.explanation: Loans to distressed persons, other than distressed farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders, of up to ₹1.00 lakh per borrower to prepay their debt to non-institutional lenders qualify under 'Others' and also count under weaker sections.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹2 lakh is the limit for SHG/JLG social-needs loans and individual women beneficiaries; ₹50,000 and ₹5 lakh are not limits for this item.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹1 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Loans to distressed persons [other than distressed farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders] not exceeding ₹1.00 lakh per borrower to prepay their debt to non-institutional lenders

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, loans to start-ups that conform to the definition of MSME qualify under the MSME category up to:

solution.explanation: Loans up to ₹50 crore to start-ups that conform to the MSME definition qualify under MSME. The same ₹50 crore limit applies to start-ups in agriculture and allied services and to start-ups under 'Others'.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹10 crore is the FPO limit; ₹100 crore the cap for agriculture infrastructure and food processing; ₹25 crore is not a start-up limit.
solution.final_answer: Option B: ₹50 crore

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to ₹50 crore to Start-ups, that conform to the definition of MSME, shall also be eligible to be classified under this category

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A farmers' producer company directly engaged in agriculture takes loans against pledge of its produce for nine months. Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, up to what amounts do such loans qualify as farm credit?

options.text: ₹90 lakh against NWRs/eNWRs and ₹75 lakh against other warehouse receipts
₹2.5 crore against NWRs/eNWRs and ₹4 crore against other warehouse receipts
₹10 crore against any kind of warehouse receipt
₹4 crore against NWRs/eNWRs and ₹2.5 crore against other warehouse receipts

solution.concept: Pledge loans to corporate farmers and FPOs
solution.explanation: For corporate farmers, FPOs/FPCs, partnership firms and co-operatives of farmers, loans against pledge or hypothecation of agricultural produce for up to 12 months qualify up to ₹4 crore against negotiable warehouse receipts (NWR/eNWR) and up to ₹2.5 crore against other warehouse receipts.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹90 lakh is the eNWR limit for individual farmers; the third option reverses the limits; ₹10 crore is the limit for FPO loans with assured marketing, not pledge loans.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹4 crore against NWRs/eNWRs and ₹2.5 crore against other warehouse receipts

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to ₹4 crore against pledge/hypothecation of agricultural produce (including warehouse receipts) for a period not exceeding 12 months against NWRs/eNWRs and up to ₹2.5 crore against warehouse receipts other than NWRs/eNWRs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Loans to Farmer Producer Organisations/Companies of individual farmers count towards the Small and Marginal Farmers (SMF) sub-target under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025 when the land-holding share of SMFs in the FPO is at least:

solution.concept: FPO loans under the SMF sub-target
solution.explanation: SMFs include loans to FPOs/FPCs of individual farmers and co-operatives of farmers directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities where the land-holding share of SMFs is not less than 75%, subject to the farm-credit loan limits.
solution.why_others_wrong: 51%, 60% and 90% are not the threshold in the Directions.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 75 per cent

fact_checks.claim: Loans to FPOs/FPCs of individual farmers and co-operatives of farmers directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities where the land-holding share of SMFs is not less than 75 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's PSL Directions (as updated) allow bank credit to the National Co-operative Development Corporation (NCDC) for on-lending to co-operative societies to be classified as priority sector. Which condition applies?

options.text: NCDC must give the lending banks quarterly certificates from a CAG-empanelled chartered accountant firm confirming the use of the credit
The loans must be guaranteed by the Government of India
Only RRBs may lend to NCDC for this purpose
The credit counts only if NCDC lends to individual farmers directly

solution.explanation: Bank credit to NCDC for on-lending to co-operative societies for eligible purposes counts under the respective PSL categories, subject to NCDC furnishing quarterly certificates by a CAG-empanelled chartered accountant firm confirming how the credit was used. The provision applies to loans sanctioned after 19 January 2026.
steps: Quarterly certificate from CAG-empanelled CA firm
Applies to loans sanctioned after 19 January 2026
solution.why_others_wrong: No Government guarantee or RRB-only rule is prescribed, and the on-lending is to co-operative societies.
solution.final_answer: Option A: NCDC must give the lending banks quarterly certificates from a CAG-empanelled chartered accountant firm confirming the use of the credit

fact_checks.claim: Bank credit to National Co-operative Development Corporation (NCDC) for on-lending to co-operative societies ... will be eligible for classification as priority sector lending ... subject to NCDC furnishing quarterly certificates by a CAG empanelled chartered accountant firm, to the lending banks, confirming that the bank credit has been utilize[d]
The provisions of para 24A are applicable to loans sanctioned by banks to NCDC after January 19, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's PSL FAQs (September 2026), what is the correct position on classifying loans under 'Weaker Sections'?

options.text: Any loan to a borrower from the listed groups qualifies, whatever its purpose
The bank must obtain a caste or community certificate for every SC/ST/Minority borrower
Weaker sections loans need not satisfy any PSL category since they form a separate target
The loan must first qualify under one of the eight PSL categories; a customer's declaration suffices for the Minority/SC/ST status

solution.explanation: For classification under weaker sections, loans should first be eligible under any of the eight PSL categories as per the underlying activity. A declaration by the customer in the application form is enough to classify credit to Minorities/SCs/STs under weaker sections.
steps: Step 2: borrower in a weaker-section group (declaration enough for Minority/SC/ST)
solution.why_others_wrong: Group membership alone is not enough; certificates are not required; weaker sections is a sub-target within PSL, not outside it.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The loan must first qualify under one of the eight PSL categories; a customer's declaration suffices for the Minority/SC/ST status

fact_checks.claim: For classification under 'Weaker Sections', the loans should first be eligible for classification under any of the eight PSL categories as per underlying activity
Declaration by the customer in the application form would suffice for classifying credit facilities to Minorities/SCs/STs under Weaker Sections

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the co-lending model (CLM) between banks and NBFCs for priority sector loans, based on RBI's PSL FAQs (September 2026):
I. If the bank can exercise its discretion on taking the NBFC-originated loans into its books, the arrangement is akin to a direct assignment transaction.
II. If the agreement entails a prior, irrevocable commitment by the bank to take its share of each loan, the arrangement is also akin to a direct assignment transaction.
III. The bilateral Master Agreement may cap the number and amount of loans the NBFC can originate under the CLM.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say only an arrangement in which the bank can exercise discretion over taking the loans is akin to direct assignment; a prior, irrevocable commitment is not. The Master Agreement governs the arrangement and may specify a cap on the number and amount of loans.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: Only if the bank can exercise its discretion regarding taking into its books the loans originated by NBFC as per the agreement, the arrangement will be akin to a direct assignment transaction. If the Agreement entails a prior, irrevocable commitment ... it shall not be akin to direct assignment transaction
The agreement may specify any cap on the number and amount of loans that can be originated by the NBFC under the Co-lending model

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Does a scheduled commercial bank need RBI's permission in each case to open a Banking Outlet in a Tier 1 centre, under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025?

options.text: Yes; permission is needed for every outlet in Tier 1 and Tier 2 centres
Yes; permission is needed for every outlet in any centre
No; banks have general permission to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres unless specifically restricted
No, but only if the outlet is manned by a Business Correspondent

solution.explanation: With financial inclusion as the overarching objective, a scheduled commercial bank may open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres without RBI permission in each case, unless specifically restricted; a bank from which general permission has been withdrawn needs prior approval.
steps: Exception: bank whose general permission is withdrawn
solution.why_others_wrong: Case-by-case permission is not required in any tier, and the permission is not limited to BC-manned outlets.
solution.final_answer: Option C: No; banks have general permission to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres unless specifically restricted

fact_checks.claim: a scheduled commercial bank is permitted to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres without having the need to obtain permission from RBI in each case, unless otherwise specifically restricted

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When RBI introduced the Business Correspondent model, banks could not collect any charges from customers for services delivered through BCs. According to RBI's discussion paper on engaging 'for-profit' companies as BCs, when were banks first allowed to collect reasonable service charges for such services?

solution.explanation: RBI's discussion paper records that, initially, banks were not allowed to collect charges for BC services; in November 2009 they were allowed to collect reasonable service charges from customers in a transparent manner under a Board-approved policy. (Today the bank, not the BC, may levy such charges.)
solution.why_others_wrong: January 2006 is when the BC model began; April 2008 brought the base-branch rules; September 2010 widened the list of eligible BCs.
solution.final_answer: Option B: November 2009

fact_checks.claim: Initially, banks were not allowed to collect any charges from the customers for providing services through BC ... Subsequently, banks were allowed in November 2009 to collect reasonable service charges from customers in a transparent manner under a Board-approved policy

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to SBI's FAQs on PMJDY, how did Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana differ from the earlier Financial Inclusion Plan ('Swabhimaan')?

options.text: Swabhimaan focused on covering villages, whereas PMJDY covers rural and urban areas, aiming at every household/adult
Swabhimaan covered only urban areas, whereas PMJDY covers only rural areas
Swabhimaan offered overdrafts, whereas PMJDY offers none
Swabhimaan was run by RBI, whereas PMJDY is run by NABARD

solution.why_others_wrong: Swabhimaan was not urban-only; PMJDY does offer an overdraft; PMJDY is run by the Department of Financial Services, not NABARD.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Swabhimaan focused on covering villages, whereas PMJDY covers rural and urban areas, aiming at every household/adult

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank uses its Business Correspondents for preliminary work in opening customer accounts. Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, who is responsible for ensuring compliance with KYC and AML norms in the BC model?

options.text: The base Banking Outlet's local Lead District Manager

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the history of the Business Correspondent model, as recorded in RBI's discussion paper on engaging 'for-profit' companies as BCs:
I. Guidelines of April 2008 required every BC to be attached to a base branch, ordinarily within 15 km in rural, semi-urban and urban areas and 5 km in metropolitan centres.
II. The Committee on Financial Inclusion (Chairman: Dr C. Rangarajan) observed that NBFCs engaged in micro finance could be recognised as BCs only for savings and remittance services.
III. From the start of the BC model in 2006, banks could levy service charges on customers for services rendered through BCs.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: The April 2008 guideline attached each BC to a base branch, ordinarily within 15 km (rural, semi-urban, urban) or 5 km (metropolitan). The Rangarajan Committee observed that micro-finance NBFCs could be BCs only for savings and remittance services, where there is no conflict of interest. Charges were not allowed at first; reasonable charges were permitted only from November 2009.
steps: III: wrong (charges allowed only from November 2009)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: every BC is required to be attached to and be under the oversight of a specific bank branch designated as the base branch. This guideline was issued in April 2008 along with the stipulation that the distance ... should not exceed 15 kms in rural, semi-urban and urban areas and 5 kms in metropolitan centers

The Committee on Financial Inclusion (Chairman: Dr C. Rangarajan) had observed that NBFCs engaged in micro finance could be recognized as BCs of banks for providing only savings and remittance services
Initially, banks were not allowed to collect any charges ... Subsequently, banks were allowed in November 2009 to collect reasonable service charges

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about grievance redressal and social audit in the Business Correspondent model under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. As a measure of social audit, there could be periodic block-level meetings of the public with BCs and linked branch managers, which the Lead District Manager could attend.
II. The bank must widely publicise the name and contact number of its designated Grievance Redressal Officer for complaints about BC services.
III. Complaints about services rendered by BCs are to be redressed by the BC company's own grievance machinery, not the bank's.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: The Directions suggest periodic block-level meetings as social audit, which the LDM could attend to get feedback. Grievance redressal machinery for BC services must be constituted within the bank and publicised, with the designated officer's name and number made known. Statement III is wrong.
steps: III: wrong (machinery is within the bank)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing III are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: As a measure of social audit, there could be periodic block level meetings where members of public are invited along with the BCs operating in the area as also the linked branch managers ... Lead District Manager (LDM) of the lead bank could attend such meetings

Grievance Redressal Machinery shall be constituted within the bank for redressing complaints for services rendered by the BCs ... The name and contact number of designated Grievance Redressal Officer of the bank shall also be made known and widely publicised

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) rules, what Required Stable Funding (RSF) factor applies to a bank's coins and banknotes and its CRR balances with RBI?

solution.explanation: Coins and banknotes immediately available to meet obligations, CRR balances (required and excess) and claims on RBI with residual maturity under six months get a zero RSF factor: they need no stable funding.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5% applies to unencumbered Level 1 assets and SLR securities; 50% and 100% apply to less liquid assets.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 0 per cent

fact_checks.claim: The following shall be assigned a zero per cent RSF factor: (1) Coins and banknotes immediately available to meet obligations; (2) CRR balances including required and excess reserves; and all claims on the RBI with residual maturities of less than six months

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Available Stable Funding (ASF) in the NSFR is the portion of a bank's capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over what time horizon?

solution.explanation: RBI defines ASF as the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over the time horizon considered by the NSFR, which extends to one year. The LCR, by contrast, looks at a 30-day stress period.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 days is the LCR horizon; three months and five years are not used.
solution.final_answer: Option C: One year

fact_checks.claim: ASF refers to the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over the time horizon considered by the NSFR, which extends to one year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In RBI's 2025 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), HDFC Bank is placed in which bucket, and what additional CET1 requirement applies to it?

solution.explanation: RBI's list released on 2 December 2025 keeps the 2024 bucketing: SBI in bucket 4 (0.80%), HDFC Bank in bucket 2 (0.40%) and ICICI Bank in bucket 1 (0.20%). Buckets 3 and 5 are empty.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bucket 1 is ICICI Bank, bucket 4 is SBI, and bucket 3 has no bank.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Bucket 2; 0.40% of risk-weighted assets

fact_checks.claim: Bucket 4 State Bank of India 0.80%; 3 - 0.60%; 2 HDFC Bank 0.40%; 1 ICICI Bank 0.20%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank under liquidity stress, having used all its other HQLA, draws funds under the Facility to Avail Liquidity for LCR (FALLCR). On what terms is this facility available?

options.text: At 200 bps above the LAF repo rate, availed or rolled over for up to 90 days
At the repo rate itself, for up to 14 days
At the Bank Rate, for up to one year
At 100 bps above the SDF rate, for up to 30 days

solution.explanation: FALLCR is available only under stress and after all other HQLA (including MSF-eligible securities) are used, with a declaration to that effect. It can be availed or rolled over for a maximum of 90 days, the securities attract MSF haircuts, and the rate is 200 bps above the prevailing LAF repo rate.
steps: Only in stress, after exhausting other HQLA
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options give tenors and rates that RBI has not prescribed for FALLCR.

Remove it from the stock on the same day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

When the account is a current account of any business entity
When the depositor's salary or pension is credited automatically, or bills are regularly paid from it under a registered mandate
When the depositor uses a debit card on it

solution.explanation: RBI treats an account as transactional if the depositor's salary or pension is automatically deposited into it, or bill payments are regularly withdrawn from it through a registered mandate (ECS/NACH, utilities, loan repayments). questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

When it forms 25% or more of the bank's HQLA
When the bank has a branch in a country using that currency
When the bank's aggregate liabilities in that currency are 5% or more of its total liabilities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Over the next 30 days a bank expects cash outflows of ₹1,000 crore and contractual inflows of ₹900 crore. Its stock of HQLA is ₹300 crore. What is its LCR under RBI's rules?

solution.explanation: Inflows can be recognised only up to 75% of outflows: min(900, 750) = 750. Net cash outflows = 1,000 − 750 = 250. LCR = 300 ÷ 250 = 120%, above the 100% minimum. Without the cap the ratio would wrongly appear as 300 ÷ 100 = 300%.

LCR shall be computed as the ratio of the stock of HQLA to the Net Cash Outflows over the next 30 calendar days

Both may launch it without any further step, since each already has an approval
P may launch it freely, but Q must seek fresh approval because its approval was channel-specific

It should not reject the transaction; both banks must maintain valid, verified LEI information after credit
It may credit the amount only if the beneficiary is an individual

solution.explanation: All single NEFT/RTGS payments of ₹50 crore and above by non-individuals must carry remitter and beneficiary LEI, and the remitting bank should ensure both are captured. But an inward transaction with inappropriate or no LEI should not be rejected by the beneficiary bank; after credit, both banks should maintain valid and verified LEI information.
steps: Missing LEI on inward → do not reject
Post-credit → both banks maintain valid LEI
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI says such transactions should not be rejected or held; a company-to-company payment is not an individual transaction.
solution.final_answer: Option C: It should not reject the transaction; both banks must maintain valid, verified LEI information after credit

fact_checks.claim: Any inward transaction with inappropriate or no LEI should not be rejected by beneficiary bank. However, post-credit, both remitting and beneficiary banks should maintain valid and verified LEI information for all payment transactions of ₹50 crore and above

All single payment transactions of ₹50 crore and above undertaken by entities (non-individuals) should include remitter and beneficiary LEI information. This is applicable to transactions undertaken through the NEFT and RTGS payment systems

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's FAQs on the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for large value transactions:
I. The LEI is a 20-character alpha-numeric code, obtainable in India from Legal Entity Identifier India Ltd.
II. In NEFT messages, the first two lines of the optional field 7495 are used to capture the sender's and the beneficiary's LEI, in that order.
III. In RTGS, the LEI requirement for payments of ₹50 crore and above applies to customer payments but not to inter-bank transactions.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The LEI is a 20-character code issued by LOUs accredited by GLEIF; in India, by LEIL (I correct). In NEFT the first two lines of field 7495 carry sender and beneficiary LEI, with narration in the last four lines (II correct). In RTGS both customer payments and inter-bank transactions of ₹50 crore and above must carry LEI (III wrong).
steps: III: RTGS inter-bank also covered → wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including III is wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is a 20-character alpha-numeric code ... In India, LEI can be obtained from Legal Entity Identifier India Ltd.
In NEFT payment messages, the field 7495 ... The first two lines of this field hall be used for capturing sender and beneficiary customer LEI information, in that order
In case of RTGS, both customer payment and inter-bank transactions meeting the above criterion should include LEI information

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT among the details a remitting customer must furnish to the bank for an RTGS remittance, according to RBI's RTGS FAQs?

options.text: The IFSC of the receiving branch
The account number to be debited

solution.explanation: The FAQs list: the account to be debited, the beneficiary bank and branch, the IFSC of the receiving branch, the beneficiary's name and account number, any sender-to-receiver information, and the sender and beneficiary LEI for eligible transactions. The beneficiary's PAN is not required.
steps: Required: debit account, beneficiary bank/branch, IFSC, beneficiary name and account, LEI if eligible
solution.why_others_wrong: IFSC, beneficiary account number and debit account are all on RBI's list.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The beneficiary's PAN

fact_checks.claim: The account number to be debited; Name of the beneficiary bank and branch; The IFSC number of the receiving branch; Name of the beneficiary customer; Account number of the beneficiary customer; Sender to receiver information, if any; Sender and Beneficiary Legal Entity Identifier (for eligible transactions)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's RTGS FAQs, where are the timelines for processing applications for the services of RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007 published?

options.text: In the RTGS System Regulations only
They are not published; each application is decided case by case

solution.concept: Service timelines under the PSS Act
solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say RBI has published a Citizens' Charter defining timelines for services offered by its departments, including those of the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007. The membership procedure itself is in the RTGS System Regulations.
solution.why_others_wrong: The RTGS Regulations give the procedure, not the departmental service timelines; NPCI has no role here.
solution.final_answer: Option A: In RBI's Citizens' Charter

fact_checks.claim: RBI has published Citizens' Charter, wherein, timelines are defined for various services offered by the respective departments. The timelines for the services offered by the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007 are available

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the LEI requirement in RTGS, based on RBI's FAQs:
I. It applies to all channels used to connect to RTGS, including thick-client, Web-API and the Payment Originator module.
II. Ministries and Departments of the Central Government must quote their LEI for RTGS payments of ₹50 crore and above.
III. In RTGS messages, the sender's and beneficiary's LEIs are captured in the first two loops of the relevant optional field.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The LEI instructions apply to all RTGS channels: thick-client, Web-API (through INFINET or another approved network) and the Payment Originator module (I correct). Governments and their Departments/Ministries need not obtain or quote LEI, though Government corporations must (II wrong). In RTGS messages the first two loops carry sender and beneficiary LEI, and narration goes in the last two (III correct).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong; 'I only' misses III.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The LEI instructions are applicable to all the channels being used for connecting to RTGS viz. thick-client, Web-API (through INFINET or any other approved network) and Payment Originator (PO) module
It is not necessary for Governments or their Departments / Ministries to obtain LEI or mention LEI number for payment transactions in NEFT and RTGS
The first two loops of this field shall be used for capturing sender and beneficiary customer LEI information, in that order

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's turn-around time (TAT) framework for failed transactions in authorised payment systems such as IMPS, how is the compensation for delay paid to the customer?

options.text: Only after the customer files a complaint with the bank
Only after the RBI Ombudsman passes an award
By NPCI directly, in cash at the bank branch
It is credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim

solution.explanation: RBI's circular of 20 September 2019 says that wherever financial compensation is involved, it must be credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim. Customers who do not get redress within the TAT can complain under RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.
solution.why_others_wrong: No complaint, Ombudsman award or cash payment by NPCI is required.
solution.final_answer: Option D: It is credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim

fact_checks.claim: Wherever financial compensation is involved, the same shall be effected to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim from the customer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which transactions are covered by RBI's harmonised turn-around time (TAT) and compensation framework for failed transactions in authorised payment systems such as IMPS and UPI?

options.text: All transactions of Indian customers, including remittances abroad
Domestic transactions, where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India
Only transactions through bank branches, not through mobile apps

solution.explanation: The framework's general instructions say it covers domestic transactions, i.e., those where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India. It applies across authorised payment systems and to non-banks wherever they are authorised to operate, with no amount threshold or channel restriction.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cross-border transactions are excluded; there is no amount threshold or channel restriction.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Domestic transactions, where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India

fact_checks.claim: Domestic transactions i.e., those where both the originator and beneficiary are within India are covered under this framework

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
RBI's TAT framework for failed transactions states two principles. Apply them to these IMPS cases:
Case 1: Asha's account is debited for a credit-push transfer, but Bina's account is not credited within the prescribed time.
Case 2: Chetan's bank delays initiating his transfer beyond the TAT.
To whom is the penalty payable in each case?

options.text: Case 1: to Asha (the originator); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)
Case 1: to Bina; Case 2: to Chetan's intended beneficiary
Case 1: to Bina (the beneficiary); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)
In both cases the penalty is paid to NPCI's customer protection fund

solution.explanation: The framework says: if a credit-push transfer is debited to the originator but the beneficiary account is not credited, credit must be given within the prescribed time, failing which the penalty is paid to the beneficiary; if there is delay in initiating the transaction at the originator bank's end beyond the TAT, the penalty is paid to the originator.
steps: Delay in credit to beneficiary → penalty to beneficiary (Bina)
Delay in initiation at originator's bank → penalty to originator (Chetan)
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options misplace the recipient of the penalty; there is no NPCI fund in the framework.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Case 1: to Bina (the beneficiary); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)

fact_checks.claim: If the transaction is a 'credit-push' funds transfer and the beneficiary account is not credited while the debit to originator has been effected, then credit is to be effected within the prescribed time period failing which the penalty has to be paid to the beneficiary; If there is delay in initiation of a transaction at the originator bank's end beyond the TAT, then penalty has to be paid to the originator

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025 require at least two factors of authentication for digital payments, with listed exemptions. Which UPI use case was added to the list of exemptions through a letter to NPCI in September 2026?

options.text: UPI person-to-person transfers to new payees
Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled point-of-sale machines
UPI payments above ₹1 lakh to hospitals

solution.explanation: Annexure-1 of the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 lists the exemptions in force, such as small-value contactless card payments, recurring e-mandate debits (other than the first), NETC transactions and small-value offline payments. It now includes Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled PoS machines, under a letter to NPCI dated 2 September 2026.
steps: Tap and Pay UPI on NFC PoS → letter of 2 September 2026
solution.why_others_wrong: The other UPI uses are not in the exemption list.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled point-of-sale machines

fact_checks.claim: Tap and Pay UPI Payment on Near Field Communication enabled Point of Sale machines Letter dated September 2, 2026 (CO.DPSS.POLC.No. S-550/02-23-001/2026-27 dated September 2, 2026) issued to NPCI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, which also governs UPI AutoPay, what must the issuer's post-transaction notification include at the minimum, besides the merchant's name, amount, date and time and reference numbers?

options.text: The reason for the debit (the e-mandate registered by the customer) and details on grievance redressal
The customer's credit score and available balance
A one-time password to confirm the debit

solution.explanation: After an e-mandate debit, the issuer must send a post-transaction notification giving at least the merchant's name, transaction amount, date and time, reference numbers of the transaction and e-mandate, the reason for the debit (the customer's registered e-mandate) and details on grievance redressal, the last added on the basis of feedback.
steps: Post-debit notice: merchant, amount, date/time, references, reason, grievance redressal details
solution.why_others_wrong: Credit score, merchant tax IDs or an OTP are not required; recurring debits after the first need no AFA within limits.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The reason for the debit (the e-mandate registered by the customer) and details on grievance redressal

fact_checks.claim: An issuer shall send a post-transaction notification to the customer. This notification shall, at the minimum, inform the customer about the merchant's name, transaction amount, date and time of debit, reference number of transaction and e-mandate, reason for debit, i.e., e-mandate registered by the customer, and details on grievance redressal

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, a customer wants to change the validity period of her UPI AutoPay mandate. What does the framework require for any modification or withdrawal of an existing e-mandate?

options.text: A written request at the home branch
Nothing; it can be changed by the merchant on the customer's request

solution.explanation: The issuer must let the customer modify the validity period or withdraw the e-mandate at any time, and any modification in, or withdrawal of, an existing e-mandate requires AFA validation by the issuer.
steps: Validated with AFA by the issuer
solution.why_others_wrong: No branch visit or merchant approval is needed, and the merchant cannot alter it.
solution.final_answer: Option D: AFA validation by the issuer

fact_checks.claim: Any modification in, or withdrawal of, an existing e-mandate shall require AFA validation by the issuer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From 1 August 2025, NPCI moved the execution of UPI AutoPay mandate debits to non-peak hours. Which periods does NPCI define as peak hours?

options.text: 8 am to 11 am and 6 pm to 10 pm
9 am to 12 noon and 4 pm to 8 pm
12 noon to 3 pm and 7 pm to 11 pm
10 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9:30 pm

solution.explanation: NPCI's May 2025 circular defines peak hours as 10:00 to 13:00 and 17:00 to 21:30, when UPI transactions reach their highest transactions per second; any other time is non-peak. AutoPay mandates can still be created at any time, but their execution is moved to non-peak hours.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other windows are not those NPCI specified.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 10 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9:30 pm

fact_checks.claim: Peak hours are defined as the period during the day when UPI financial transactions reach the highest transactions per second, observed from 10:00 hrs (10 am) to 13:00 hrs (1 pm) and from 17:00 hrs (5 pm) to 21:30 hrs (9.30 pm)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, how is interoperability across PPIs issued in the form of wallets to be enabled?

options.text: Through the RuPay card network only
Through the Bharat Bill Payment System

solution.explanation: The PPI Master Direction says that where PPIs are issued as wallets, interoperability across PPIs shall be enabled through UPI; PPIs in the form of cards achieve interoperability through authorised card networks. Since *99# USSD is part of UPI, non-bank PPI issuers may also participate in it.
solution.why_others_wrong: Card networks serve card PPIs; NEFT and BBPS are not the interoperability route for wallets.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Through UPI

fact_checks.claim: Where PPIs are issued in the form of wallets, interoperability across PPIs shall be enabled through UPI
Since *99# USSD is part of UPI, non-bank PPI issuer are also allowed to participate in the same

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about UPI payments from PPIs under RBI's Master Direction on PPIs:
I. A UPI payment from a PPI made on the issuer's own application is authenticated using the customer's existing PPI credentials.
II. If the PPI is linked to a third-party UPI application, the payment is authenticated using UPI credentials.
III. A PPI issuer acting as a PSP may onboard customers of any bank onto its UPI handle.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: On the issuer's own app, UPI transactions from a PPI use the existing PPI credentials and are thus pre-approved before reaching UPI (I correct). A full-KYC PPI discovered on a third-party UPI app is authenticated with UPI credentials (II correct). A PPI issuer, as PSP, shall not onboard customers of any bank or other PPI issuer (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: UPI transactions from PPI on the issuer's application shall be authenticated using the customer's existing PPI credentials ... A PPI issuer, in its capacity as a PSP, shall not on-board customers of any bank or any other PPI issuer
Such UPI transactions, from PPIs using third party UPI applications, shall be authenticated using the UPI credentials

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Neha's UPI Lite balance is ₹1,700. Under RBI's current limits for UPI Lite, (a) what is the most she can add right now, and (b) after topping up fully, what is the minimum number of UPI Lite payments needed to pay ₹4,600 to a merchant entirely from UPI Lite?

solution.explanation: The UPI Lite balance cannot exceed ₹5,000 at any time, so she can add at most ₹5,000 − ₹1,700 = ₹3,300 (online, with AFA). Each UPI Lite payment is capped at ₹1,000, so ₹4,600 needs at least ⌈4,600 ÷ 1,000⌉ = 5 payments.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 payments can carry at most ₹4,000; ₹5,000 ignores the existing balance; ₹300 and 10 use the general offline limits of ₹2,000 and ₹500.
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a) ₹3,300; (b) 5

fact_checks.claim: For UPI Lite, the enhanced limits shall be ₹1,000 per transaction with ₹5,000 being the total limit. Replenishment of used limit shall be allowed only in online mode with AFA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Bharat Bill Payment System Directions, 2024, what must happen before a bill payment is initiated through BBPS (other than for prepaid services)?

options.text: The biller must send a paper bill to the customer
The customer must visit an agent outlet

solution.explanation: The Directions describe BBPS, operated by NPCI's subsidiary NBBL, as an integrated platform for paying bills through multiple channels and modes; transactions require the bill to be fetched before payment initiation, while for prepaid services the customer's relationship with the biller is validated through the platform.
solution.why_others_wrong: Paper bills, agent visits or NPCI approval of each payment are not required.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The bill must be fetched

fact_checks.claim: The transactions facilitated through this platform will require the bill to be fetched before payment initiation. In case of transactions involving payments for prepaid services, the customer relationship with the biller will be validated through the platform

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, for which of the following e-mandates is the issuer NOT required to send a pre-transaction notification before the debit?

options.text: E-mandates for credit card bill payments
E-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) balances

solution.explanation: Issuers must normally send a pre-transaction notification at least 24 hours before an e-mandate debit, but it is not required for e-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and NCMC balances.
solution.why_others_wrong: SIPs, insurance premiums and credit card bills have a higher AFA-free limit but still need pre-debit notices.
solution.final_answer: Option D: E-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) balances

fact_checks.claim: Pre-transaction notification is not required for e-mandates registered to auto-replenish balances of FASTag, and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025) describe the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)?

options.text: A card-based system in which customers use RuPay debit cards at ATMs
A non-bank wallet system regulated as a prepaid payment instrument
A bank-led model for interoperable financial inclusion transactions at micro-ATM terminals through Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication
A system for bulk credit of salaries operated by UIDAI

solution.explanation: RBI describes AePS as a bank-led model that facilitates online interoperable financial inclusion transactions at PoS (micro-ATM) terminals through banks' Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication; UIDAI verifies biometrics and NPCI handles switching, clearing and settlement.
steps: AePS: bank-led, BC micro-ATMs, Aadhaar authentication
solution.why_others_wrong: AePS is not card-based or a wallet system, and UIDAI does not operate a bulk-credit system.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A bank-led model for interoperable financial inclusion transactions at micro-ATM terminals through Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication

fact_checks.claim: Aadhaar-enabled Payment System (AePS) is a bank-led model that facilitates online interoperable financial inclusion transactions at Point of Sale (Micro ATM) terminals through Business Correspondents of banks, using Aadhaar authentication

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's framework on turn-around time for failed transactions, there is a delay in crediting a beneficiary's account through the Aadhaar Payments Bridge System (APBS), used for government benefits. What must be done?

options.text: The remitting government department must re-send the payment within T + 5 days
The beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day, with ₹100 per day of delay beyond that
NPCI must credit the beneficiary from its own funds within T + 3 days
No time limit applies, as APBS payments are government transfers

solution.explanation: For APBS, where there is a delay in crediting the beneficiary's account, the beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day; compensation of ₹100 per day applies if the delay goes beyond T + 1.
steps: APBS credit delay → beneficiary bank reverses by T + 1
solution.why_others_wrong: The framework places the duty on the beneficiary bank, not the department or NPCI, and APBS is covered.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day, with ₹100 per day of delay beyond that

fact_checks.claim: Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS) a Delay in crediting beneficiary's account. Beneficiary bank to reverse the transaction within T + 1 day. ₹100/- per day if delay is beyond T + 1 day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS) under RBI's BBPS Directions, 2024, operated by NPCI's subsidiary NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL):
I. A non-bank BBPOU must open an escrow account with a scheduled commercial bank exclusively for BBPS transactions.
II. A sponsor bank, which is a scheduled commercial bank, facilitates settlement of non-bank BBPOUs with NBBL.
III. A Customer Operating Unit (COU) is the entity that onboards billers onto the BBPS platform.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Non-bank BBPOUs must keep an escrow account with an SCB exclusively for BBPS (I correct). A sponsor bank (an SCB) facilitates their settlement with NBBL (II correct). Billers are onboarded by a Biller Operating Unit (BOU); a COU provides customers the interface to pay bills (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III confuse COU and BOU; 'II only' misses I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: A non-bank BBPOU shall open an escrow account with a Scheduled Commercial Bank exclusively for BBPS transactions
Sponsor bank: A Scheduled Commercial Bank which facilitates settlement of non-bank BBPOUs with NBBL
Biller Operating Unit (BOU) is an entity which onboards biller(s) ... Customer Operating Unit (COU) is an entity which provides its customers with an interface (physical / digital) to pay bills
